title: Coupled-channel scattering from artificial confinement
authors: Tafat Weiss Attia, Itay Horin, Betzalel Bazak
abstract: Artificial confinement encodes continuum scattering information in discrete, bound-state-like spectra, allowing reaction observables to be extracted with finite-basis or finite-domain methods. We apply this strategy to a two-channel cluster model of $^4$He with open $^3$H+p and $^3$He+n channels. We extract coupled-channel observables from spectra generated by a harmonic-oscillator (HO) trap, a spherical hard wall, and, within a single-partial-wave truncation, a periodic cubic box. The three geometries are formulated in a unified quantization-condition framework and benchmarked against a continuum $R$-matrix calculation. Above the second-channel threshold, several confined levels at a common scattering energy are combined in an overdetermined fit to determine two phase shifts and an inelasticity. Without Coulomb interactions, all three geometries yield consistent results for the $^1S_0$ and $^3P_1$ partial waves. With Coulomb interactions in the charged $^3$H+p channel, the HO and spherical-wall results also agree closely with the continuum reference. A Monte Carlo propagation study shows that spectral uncertainties are amplified near trap-function poles and along poorly conditioned directions associated with the inelasticity and phase-shift difference, whereas the phase-shift sum remains comparatively robust. These results provide a controlled benchmark for confinement-based scattering methods and delineate their strengths and limitations for future few-body and ab initio reaction calculations.
summary: This paper develops a methodology to extract continuum scattering parameters (phase shifts and inelasticity) for a Helium cluster model by fitting multiple discrete energy levels obtained from different artificial confinement potentials (HO, hard wall, box). The results confirm the consistency of these methods when compared to a continuum R-matrix calculation, while also quantifying the sensitivity of the extracted observables to spectral noise and the specific confinement geometry used.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical challenge of extracting continuum scattering information, which is defined by asymptotic wave functions, from discrete, bound-state-like spectra generated by finite-basis or finite-domain calculations.
main_result: The study demonstrates that multiple confinement geometries (HO, hard wall, cubic box) yield consistent results for scattering observables when fitted using an overdetermined approach, providing a controlled benchmark for such methods.
method: The authors employ a unified quantization-condition framework, fitting multiple confined energy levels at a common scattering energy to determine coupled-channel observables like phase shifts and inelasticity.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a two-channel cluster model of Helium-4, involving open channels like $^3	ext{H}+	ext{p}$ and $^3	ext{He}+	ext{n}$, and includes long-range Coulomb interactions in one channel.
key_observables: Two-channel phase shifts ($\delta_1, \delta_2$) and the inelasticity ($\eta$).
important_parameters: The comparison is made across three confinement geometries: Harmonic-Oscillator (HO) trap, spherical hard wall, and periodic cubic box.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that matching the number of usable constraints across different geometries allows for a fair comparison, and it notes that spectral uncertainties are amplified near trap-function poles.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the extracted observables (e.g., $3P_1$ partial wave) across different geometries compared to the R-matrix reference, and show the propagation of spectral uncertainties for different traps.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by comparing confinement methods (HO, hard wall, box) against a continuum R-matrix benchmark. It then details the fitting procedure using multiple energy crossings to extract the three key scattering parameters, concluding with a detailed analysis of the stability and limitations of each confinement geometry.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a rigorous, quantitative benchmark for using artificial confinement potentials to calculate fundamental scattering properties in few-body and nuclear physics systems, which is a key area for theoretical AMO/open quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Coupled-channel 1S0 spectra for the three confine- ment geometries. From top to bottom, the panels show the discrete energies as functions of the oscillator energy ℏω, periodic-box length L, and spherical-wall radius R. Each curve represents one confined level. PCHIP interpolation of the individual curves locates the confinement parameters at which several levels cross a common scattering energy.

FIG. 2. Inelasticity and phase shifts in the 1S0 partial wave as functions of scattering energy. The left panel omits the Coulomb interaction, while the right panel includes it in the charged 3H + p channel. In each panel, the upper plot shows η(E) and the lower plot shows δ1(E) and δ2(E). Black curves are the R-matrix reference; colored symbols are the observables extracted from the HO trap (red), spherical hard wall (blue), and periodic cubic box (green). Periodic-box results are not included in the calculation with Coulomb interactions.
